speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: asked	the Minister for Home Affairs (a) whether families of death row inmates can be provided with at least three weeks' notice before the sentence is carried out to allow them sufficient time to come to terms with the sentence and make necessary arrangements; (b) what processes are in place to help such families deal with the trauma of the loss of their loved ones; and (c) whether family members of death row inmates can be allowed to have physical contact during the last few visits after the date of execution has been set.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Throughout the inmates' stay in prison, families visit the inmates and also communicate with them.

speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Home Affairs (Mr Desmond Lee) (for the Minister for Home Affairs)
text: Inmates are also notified at every stage of the legal and clemency process.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: The reason for asking for a longer notice period is to give the families sufficient time to make the necessary preparations, as well as for the grief process.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: At the moment, they will be informed on Monday, and usually Tuesdays to Thursdays are when the extended visits are allowed.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: So, I am asking whether it could be extended a bit more so that they would have more time to deal with that process.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: The second supplementary question is that I understand that some death row inmates' family members would be grateful for just one opportunity to be able to have that physical contact.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: In fact, the Government has made an exception once to permit one death row inmate's mother's physical contact, to hold the hands of her son.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun (Nominated Member)
text: So, would the Ministry consider granting this possibility during the last visits, if the family members and the death row inmates so desire?

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: But as I have said in my reply earlier, between conviction and the actual carrying out of the sentence, there is a certain duration of time.

speaker: Mr Desmond Lee
text: Throughout that duration, families and next-of-kin are given opportunities to communicate and to visit the inmates.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: So, yes, if the family members do ask for the opportunity for physical contact, the Singapore Prison Service would consider.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: So, they could put up an application or ask for it.

speaker: Mr Kok Heng Leun
text: So, this is the period that we need to give them a bit more time and space to handle the process.
